requirements.requirement: Local logging on node1 remains functional and its data survives a restart.
requirements.summary: Before restart, syslog and cron were healthy and both live and archived markers were readable. The reboot was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and afterward syslog and cron recovered, the pre-reboot live marker and compressed archive remained readable, and a new marker was logged successfully.

requirements.requirement: Local logs are retained for 14 days without unbounded archive growth.
requirements.summary: Logrotate parsed a daily policy retaining 14 rotations and removing archives older than 14 days. Cron was enabled and running, an actual compressed rotation preserved archived data and continued live logging, and the policy, scheduler, archive, and executable daily job remained healthy after reboot. The rotation count bounds archive accumulation.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol for node1 was complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, independently corroborated boot-ID change, and recovered services, policy, live data, and archived data. Only minor cleanup residue affects operational hygiene.
limitations: Retention was not observed across 14 elapsed days; the assessment relies on the parsed policy, active daily scheduler, successful real rotation, and successful post-reboot scheduler invocation.
The lifecycle failed-services probe was unsupported on Alpine, although the task-relevant OpenRC syslog and crond services were directly checked before and after restart.
The final existence of /etc/conf.d/syslog.pre-retention was not directly checked; its creation and absence of any captured cleanup are the available evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: The package installation, configuration changes, service operations, test markers, forced rotation, and reboot all had clear task or verification roles. Minor unnecessary retained residue remained: /tmp/logrotate-debug.out from cmd-222bf55271484509 and /tmp/[REDACTED].log from cmd-546bb49fde214a7a were confirmed after execution. A precautionary /etc/conf.d/syslog.pre-retention backup was created by cmd-3c1119f68d0b47ed and no removal was captured; its final presence was not directly inventoried. None of these residues was shown reverted. No additional listening exposure or package-health degradation was observed relative to baseline.
